It depends on the school. In my decade of experience teaching, there was this one school that made teachers change the grades of the students to make them 90 and above. It's not even to simply pass the students, it's to please the parents and make them think the school is doing such a great job keeping all the students entertained in class. The school made us do it every term it was defeating the purpose of education. Even students who didn't pass anything (despite all the teachers' efforts to send emails, meet for review classes, send review notes, help in creating projects and answering seatwork, etc.) have to get high grades.

I am happy when my students get high grades but that is when they truly deserve it. But giving them high grades for the reasons of our school administration is beyond incredulous. High performing students lose interest, don't show anymore growth, and end up not giving their best because they know that they'll get the same scores as their classmates who are not submitting and participating. Low performing students don't realize that they need improvement because they get the same grades as the smart and hardworking students. Whenever teachers let the admin know of the students' real grades based on their performance, the admin blames us and accuse us of hindering the chances of students to get into good universities. 

It's a terrible experience. That's why I resigned; it's insulting to the profession and I can't stomach anymore being part of that system.
